Below is the full 12‑week, coachable summary of the strength + hypertrophy programme you asked for (start date 2026‑06‑01), including: the 3 phases, week-by-week focus, a daily session outline (exercises, sets/reps, intensity targets), nutrition for hypertrophy, cardio (LISS + weekly HIIT), a weekly plyometric/power day, and the 1RM test plan at the end. Phase 2 has the pushed intensity per your request and the program includes the HIIT and plyo sessions integrated to minimise interference. Use this as your master reference and adapt small details to the client’s responses during the cycle.

Format and assumptions
- Client: 26F, recreational lifter on combined OCP, full intensity clearance, good responder.
- Frequency: 4 lifting days/week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B) + 1 plyo/power session/week + 1 HIIT session/week + optional 1 LISS session/week. Total active days typically 5–6 with at least 1 full rest day.
- Start: Week 1 begins Monday 2026‑06‑01 (training days example align Monday → Sunday).
- Progression: 3 phases of 4 weeks each. Week 4, Week 8, Week 12 are lighter/deliberate reduced-volume weeks (Week 6 is an intensity-peak within Phase 2).
- Intensity guidance: use RPE when helpful. Main lifts: Phase 1 (RPE 7–8), Phase 2 (RPE 8–9 with peak singles in week 6), Phase 3 (RPE 8–9 for doubles/singles, lower volume).
- Rest between sets: main lifts 2.5–5 min; secondary heavy 2–3 min; accessory 60–90s.
- Equipment assumed: rack, barbell, plates, bench, DBs, cables, pull-up bar, sled/bike/rower.

Quick weekly layout (repeat each week unless noted)
- Mon — Upper A (Heavy / intensity)
- Tue — Lower A (Heavy / intensity)
- Wed — Plyometric / Power session (mainly morning) + mobility (HIIT placed here mid-week as described) — alternate options described below
- Thu — Upper B (Moderate / speed / hypertrophy)
- Fri — Lower B (Moderate / deadlift or posterior-chain emphasis)
- Sat — Optional LISS (20–40 min) or rest
- Sun — Rest

Cardio integration
- LISS: 2×/week optional; recommended 1 LISS on weekend 30–40 min if energy allows.
- HIIT: 1×/week (Wed preferred). Beginner → Intermediate → Advanced progressions provided (30 min total including warm-up).
- During heavy-intensity weeks (esp Week 6), reduce or omit HIIT (replace with short LISS or mobility).

Plyo/Power integration
- 1×/week on Wed (morning recommended). Keep ground contacts limited; progress from technical low-impact in Phase 1 to higher-intensity power work in Phase 2, maintain in Phase 3. Reduce volume in heavy weeks as advised.

Nutrition summary (hypertrophy)
- Calorie surplus: +250 kcal/day above maintenance (adjust +150 to +350 depending preference).
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (aim ~2.0 g/kg).
- Carbs: 3–4 g/kg/day (higher around training days).
- Fat: 20–30% calories (~0.8–1.0 g/kg/day).
- Creatine 3–5 g/day, protein powder as needed, vitamin D/omega-3 optional.
- Add 100–200 kcal and ~20–50 g extra carbs on very heavy days (Phase 2 intensity days) and on HIIT day when intense.

Week-by-week plan (detailed summary)

Phase 1 — Base (Weeks 1–4). Goal: technique, work capacity, build hypertrophy base.
Notes: Week 4 = reduced volume (~15–25% fewer sets).

Week 1 (2026‑06‑01 week) — Base introduction
Mon — Upper A (Heavy)
- Bench press: 4×5 @ RPE 7–8
- Barbell row: 4×6–8
- Overhead press: 3×6–8
- Incline DB press: 3×8–10
- Lat pulldown/pull-ups: 3×8–10
- Face pulls: 3×12–15
- Core: Plank 3×30–60s

Tue — Lower A (Heavy)
- Back squat: 4×5 @ RPE 7–8
- RDL: 4×6–8
- Bulgarian split squat: 3×8–10/leg
- Hip thrust: 3×8–10
- Hamstring curl: 3×10–12
- Calf raises: 3×12–15
- Core: Dead bug 3×10–12/side

Wed — Plyo/Power (Phase 1)
- Med ball chest pass: 3–4×4
- CMJ: 4×4
- Standing broad jump: 3×5
- Single-leg hops (reactive): 3×6/leg
- Trap bar/goblet jump (light): 3×4
- Mobility/cooldown

Thu — Upper B (Volume/Speed)
- Speed or paused bench: 8×3 @ ~60% (focus bar speed)
- Pull-ups: 4×AMRAP or 4×6–8
- Seated DB press: 3×10–12
- Chest-supported row: 3×10–12
- Lateral raises: 3×12–15
- Biceps: 3×10–12

Fri — Lower B (Volume/posterior focus)
- Deadlift: 4×4–6 @ RPE 7
- Front squat/goblet: 3×8–10
- Walking lunges: 3×10–12/leg
- Single-leg RDL: 3×8–10/leg
- Calves seated: 3×12–15

Sat — Optional LISS 25–35 min or rest

Week 2–3
- Repeat similar structure; increment loads conservatively per progression rule (if all reps completed at target RPE, add 2.5–5% where appropriate). Keep focus on form.

Overview and key principles
- Test main lifts across two days separated by at least 48–72 hours (e.g., Squat & Overhead Press on Day 1, Deadlift & Bench Press on Day 2). This spacing reduces CNS and local fatigue and gives better true maxes.
- Use a taper in Week 12 (already planned) — reduce volume by ~25–30% and limit high RPE sets prior to test days.
- Prioritise full recovery, sleep, carbohydrates, hydration, and warm-up protocols on test days.
- Use conservative attempt progression: warm-up ramp, then graded single attempts increasing by small increments. Stop testing that lift if form breaks down or bar speed drops markedly.
- Have a competent spotter or coach present for bench and squat heavy singles; use safety pins and belts appropriately.
- Record successful attempts and RPE, bar speed if available, and how it felt subjectively.

Suggested test week schedule (example)
- Day -3 (72 hrs before first test day): Heavy back-off / mobility day — very light technique work only (e.g., 2–3 sets at RPE 6), plus mobility. No heavy singles.
- Day -2 (48 hrs before first test day): Rest, flexibility, sleep prioritised; light walk or mobility only.
- Test Day 1 (e.g., Thursday of Week 12): Squat 1RM and Overhead Press 1RM (upper body after adequate rest) — heavy focus on lower-body early in the day.
- Rest 48–72 hrs (active recovery and mobility; keep protein and carbs high).
- Test Day 2 (e.g., Sunday of Week 12): Deadlift 1RM and Bench Press 1RM (do bench later in the day after adequate rest).

Alternative ordering (some coaches prefer Bench with Squat day and Deadlift with OHP day). Pick whichever works best for your athlete’s recovery and logistics. I prefer keeping deadlift and bench separate to avoid pressing fatigue after heavy deadlifts.

Pre-test nutrition and recovery (days leading up)
- Calories: Maintain the hypertrophy surplus through test week. On test days add ~100–200 kcal extra carbs pre- and post-session to top up glycogen.
- Carbs: Eat a carb-forward dinner the night before each test day (e.g., rice/potato/pasta) and a 40–80 g carb meal 60–90 minutes pre-lift.
- Protein: 25–40 g protein pre or post session; keep daily protein at ~2.0–2.2 g/kg.
- Hydration: Drink water consistently; include electrolytes if needed.
- Sleep: Aim for 8+ hours the night before each test day.
- Caffeine: 100–300 mg 30–60 min pre-test if tolerated (helps CNS readiness).

Testing logistics and safety
- Environment: quiet gym, rack with safety pins, calibrated plates if possible.
- Equipment: lifting belt, wrist wraps (if usual), DBs/plates for warm-ups, chalk if allowed, capable spotter for squat/bench.
- Warm-up ramp: dynamic warm-up + progressive sets as below — don’t rush, give 2–4 minutes rest between heavy singles, 3–5 minutes between near-max attempts.
- Stopping rules: stop the test if:
  - Technique breaks (depth for squat, hip hinging for deadlift, pressing path collapse for bench/OHP),
  - Bar speed is excessively slow (indicator of true near-max but safety concern),
  - The lifter requests to stop or feels sharp pain/discomfort.
- Attempt increments: use conservative jumps, smaller for upper body (1.25–2.5 kg) and slightly larger for lower body (2.5–5 kg). If a lift feels very close and the lifter is confident, a slightly larger jump is acceptable but avoid chasing big jumps after an initial miss.

Detailed session protocols

Test Day 1 — Squat 1RM + Overhead Press 1RM
- Order: Squat 1RM first (lower-body CNS priority), then OHP after a longer rest (1.5–2 hours if possible) or at least 30–60 minutes of light activity and mobility between tests.
- Warm-up (general 10 min):
  - 5 min light cardio (bike/walk) and dynamic mobility (hip circles, leg swings, ankle mobility, thoracic rotations).
  - Activation: Glute bridges x 2 × 8–10, banded lateral walks x 2 × 10, bodyweight squats x 2 × 5.

  - Empty bar x 10
  - 40% x 5
  - 60% x 3
  - 75% x 2
  - 85% x 1
  - 92–95% x 1 (judge gauge)
  - Attempt 1RM (single)
  - If successful and feeling good, rest 3–5 min and add 2.5–5 kg for next attempt until failure or until satisfied.
- Squat attempt guidance:
  - Use consistent commands, depth standard, and safety pins set appropriately.
  - If miss is technique related (rise on toes, knees collapse, insufficient depth), consider a second attempt at the same weight after addressing cueing — avoid immediate big jump.
- Post-squat cool-down: light walk, mobility, rehydrate.

- Overhead Press warm-up and ramp (after appropriate rest):
  - Light shoulder mobility and banded pull-aparts.
  - Empty bar x 8
  - 40% x 5
  - 60% x 3
  - 75% x 2
  - 85% x 1
  - Attempt 1RM single(s) with 3–4 min rests between top attempts.
  - Small increments (1.25–2.5 kg) on upper body.

Test Day 2 — Deadlift 1RM + Bench Press 1RM
- Order: Deadlift 1RM first (if you want maximal deadlift without pre-fatigue), then Bench Press after adequate rest (30–90 min).
- Warm-up (general 10 min):
  - 5 min easy bike/row and dynamic mobility (hip hinges, thoracic mobility)
  - Activation: glute bridges, band hamstring curls, scapular pull-ups (2 × 8–10)
- Deadlift ramp (examples):

  - 40% x 5
  - 60% x 3
  - 75% x 2
  - 85% x 1
  - 92–95% x 1
  - Attempt 1RM single
  - If successful and well-recovered, add 2.5–5 kg for next attempts with 3–5 min rest
- Deadlift attempt cues:
  - Tight core, braced breath, engaged lats, drive through legs, control lockout.
  - If miss is due to poor setup or rounding, consider re-attempt after technical cueing rather than an immediate larger jump.
- Bench Press warm-up and ramp (after rest):
  - Shoulder warm-up and banded activation.
  - Empty bar x 10
  - 40% x 5
  - 60% x 3
  - 75% x 2
  - 85% x 1
  - Attempt 1RM singles with at least 3–4 min rest between top attempts.
  - Use small increments (1.25–2.5 kg) on bench.

Attempt progression examples (practical)
- If estimated 1RM known, use ramp sets to reach ~90–95% before first 1RM attempt. If no estimated 1RM, use a conservative ramp until a heavy single is reached.
- Typical progression after hitting a heavy successful single:
  - Lower body: +2.5–5 kg increments (depending on lifter)
  - Upper body: +1.25–2.5 kg increments
- Limit to 3–5 maximal attempts per lift to avoid over-fatigue.

Recording results and follow-up
- Record:
  - Weight attempted and whether successful
  - RPE for top set
  - Bar speed if available (measure concentric velocity)
  - Notes on technique and subjective readiness
- Compare to baseline (start of Week 1 estimated 1RMs or best training numbers). Calculate % increases and note which lifts improved most.
- Use results to update training loads for the next cycle. For example, set new training maxes at 90–95% of tested 1RM (or use conservative 93% conversion) to plan percentages for the next program.

Sample conservative testing cadence (if nervous about CNS fatigue)

- Test Day 2 (48–72 hrs later): Deadlift and Overhead press

Troubleshooting misses
- If two consecutive attempts fail at the same weight, stop testing that lift for the day and schedule a reassessment in a few weeks.
- If a miss is technical (depth, bar path), consider re-attempting after cueing and a longer rest, but if fatigue is present, postpone.

Post-test recovery and next steps
